messages:
Jules (customer): hey team — our rerank endpoint started returning 504s and 5xxs under load this morning, p95 latency jumped from ~320ms to 6-9s. Happening intermittently but pretty high impact for our search UX. request_id: rq-4f7a9e
Aisha (support): sorry you're hitting this, Jules. can you paste a sample request payload (sanitized) and any request_id you saw? also which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)?
Jules (customer): hosted. sample: `POST /v1/rerank` body:
```
{"query":"how to reset password","candidates":["reset password steps","password change flow", ... 120 items ...],"top_k":5}
```
We were sending ~100-120 candidates per request, avg token length ~60 per candidate. Headers we saw: `x-request-id: rq-4f7a9e`, `x-retry-after` not present.
Aisha (support): thanks. tagging infra/eng-runtime for triage — @Marco @Priya @Elena
Marco (eng-runtime): looking. quick hypothesis: reranker is a cross-encoder model so latency scales with (#candidates * candidate_tokens). 100+ candidates * 60 tokens each = heavy. p95 jump sounds like queueing/backpressure in the frontend or gateway timeouts. can you DM the raw request_id and timestamp?
Jules (customer): sent DM with rq-4f7a9e and a couple more ids (rq-4f7a9f, rq-4f7aa0). spikes are during peak traffic, concurrency ~80 req/s.
Priya (eng-sre): pulling infra metrics now. I'm seeing a cluster-scale CPU/GPU saturation signal around the same minute as rq-4f7a9e. Also multiple `502` / `504` from our api-gateway logs with upstream timeout: `upstream_status:504`, `upstream_response_time` > 30s in some traces.
InfraBot: Deploy event: `deploy/frontend-service` completed 2025-11-14T09:08:40Z by deploy-bot. No config changes flagged.
Elena (eng-ml): adding context — the reranker model we currently serve is a cross-encoder (cross-rank-1) that runs single-pass scoring over concatenated query+candidate. It's compute intensive and latency ~O(m * L) where m = candidates. With m=100 and L=60 tokens it's expected to jump. We usually recommend <=50 candidates for this model or a bi-encoder pre-filter.
Aisha (support): immediate mitigation for customer: reduce candidate count to <=50 and add client-side exponential backoff on 5xx/504 (start 200ms -> 1s). Also set a request timeout on your HTTP client to abort long waits. Can we confirm if changing candidate count reduces errors?
Jules (customer): we can try dropping to 40, might affect quality. any server-side short-term fixes?
Marco (eng-runtime): short term we can: 1) increase the gateway upstream timeout from 30s -> 60s (not ideal), 2) route rerank traffic to a dedicated pool with more GPU concurrency if tenant qualifies, 3) enable autoscaler to add more instances faster. But we need to be careful about cost and risk.
Priya (eng-sre): I can temporarily bump the gateway timeout for the rerank route and monitor. will also open an autoscaler policy check for this customer pool.
Elena (eng-ml): long term we should offer a `pre-filter` + `rerank` pattern in docs: run cheap embed/bm25 prefilter to reduce candidates to 50, then cross-rank. Also provide guidance on `max_candidates` and example code.
Marco (eng-runtime): for triage we need: exact payload sizes, candidate token distribution, concurrency profile (rps) and if retries were enabled client-side. can you attach a couple sample request_ids and full traces?
Jules (customer): attached logs in DM. look for rq-4f7a9e, rq-4f7a9f, rq-4f7aa0 (all between 09:12:03-09:13:20).
Priya (eng-sre): got them. traces show gateway sent request to runtime but runtime returned 500 with error `model-inference-timeout` before the gateway 504 for some requests. stack: `runtime -> model-worker -> tf-runtime`. Model-worker logs show `OOM` spikes for some workers when candidate_count > 80.
Elena (eng-ml): OOM indicates peak memory pressure from long concatenated sequences. two mitigations: lower candidate_count or use float16/quantized model that reduces memory per token. We have a quantized reranker variant (cross-rank-1-q4) we can enable for hosted customers as fallback. Quality regression is small in our tests.
Aisha (support): plan from support side: advise customer to drop candidates to <=50 for now, enable client retries with jitter, monitor. I'll follow up when infra changes land.
Marco (eng-runtime): repro steps for our infra to reproduce locally: run this python script (simplified):
```
import requests, json, threading
PAYLOAD = {"query":"q","candidates":["long token sequence..." for _ in range(100)],"top_k":5}
for _ in range(80):
  threading.Thread(target=lambda: requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer X'}, json=PAYLOAD, timeout=60)).start()
```
That should emulate 80 concurrent requests with 100 candidates each. also run with `TF_FORCE_GPU_ALLOW_GROWTH=1` to capture memory behavior.
Priya (eng-sre): I'll spin up a load test using k6 with gradually increasing concurrency to trigger the p95 spike and gather metrics (gpu_util, memory_used, queue_length). will correlate with gateway traces.
Elena (eng-ml): also test with `top_k=5` vs `top_k=1` — top_k doesn't change scoring cost much but smaller top_k reduces post-processing. switch to `cross-rank-1-q4` variant in the routing table for low-latency fallback and gauge quality delta.
Jules (customer): ok will try reducing candidates and report. curious: any quick config we can toggle on hosted to avoid 5xx right now?
Marco (eng-runtime): short answer: we can route this tenant to the quantized variant or to a dedicated pool — require a short config change and brief restart of the routing proxy (2-3min). Priya can do autoscaler tuning.
Priya (eng-sre): I'm enabling a temporary routing override to use cross-rank-1-q4 for this tenant starting now. will watch for errors and revert after 2 hours if stable.
InfraBot: Routing override applied for tenant-id: t-9a1b2c to model: cross-rank-1-q4 by Priya at 2025-11-14T09:28:10Z
Marco (eng-runtime): follow-up items for eng: 1) add explicit `max_candidates` enforcement at gateway with a 400 response and doc pointer, 2) expose candidate_count metrics per-request in tracing, 3) ensure the runtime returns `Retry-After` header or `x-retryable` hint for 5xx so clients can better throttle.
Elena (eng-ml): engineering/ML follow-ups: provide an official prefilter+rerank pattern in docs, publish throughput vs candidate_count matrix for cross-rank models, and add a lightweight bi-encoder option for high-candidate scenarios.
Aisha (support): documented mitigation steps for Jules and added troubleshooting checklist to the ticket: sample payload, token counts, reduce candidates, enable client retries, request routing override (done), follow up in 1h. :thumbsup:
Jules (customer): after switching to 40 candidates + client retries errors dropped to near-zero. p95 is back to ~340ms. thanks all. we'll evaluate prefiltering to keep quality.
Marco (eng-runtime): great. leaving this thread open until we push the gateway candidate-check and metric changes. tagging follow-ups in our backlog. thanks everyone. :rocket:
